notes: Summary: Stellaris runs low-latency trading support chat + compliance reranking. Heavy supply of short queries (<= 50 tokens) and occasional long summarization batches (2-5k tokens).
Workshop objective: baseline QPS, tokens/sec profile, steady-state vs peak planning, reserved GPU recommendation for SLA-backed throughput.
Baseline observed (from sampling & app logs): steady-state 110 QPS (median request ~22 tokens in + 28 tokens out), token rate ~7k tokens/sec sustained during business hours.
Peaks: cron-driven batch jobs and market open spikes push short-duration QPS to ~620 QPS; 95th percentile token/sec bursts hit ~42k tokens/sec for 90-120s windows.
Latency SLOs: goal 95th <= 120ms for chat; p50 <= 45ms. Business priority: p95 must be stable during steady-state; 1-2s acceptable for rare peak fallback.
Model preference: primarily 7B–13B family (LLM-v1 family) for production chat + a trimmed 70B quantized variant for reranking. Interested in Redwood-verified quantized profiles.
Security & compliance notes: must support customer-managed KMS, SSO SAML integration, audit logs retained 1yr, data residency in us-east-1 for trading data.
From CTO (quote): 'We need deterministic unit economics — if you commit throughput we need clear fallbacks and predictable token pricing in SLA.'
Workshop output (actions): run an end-to-end POC: 72-hour soak test on Dedicated pool with Canary routing, simulate 3x business-hour burst, measure token/sec vs latency curve.

Sizing recommendation (workshop draft): reserve capacity to cover steady-state plus 30% buffer = target baseline 145 QPS steady -> recommended 8 x H100-80GB equivalent nodes (batching + KV cache) OR 12 x A100-80GB depending on SKU mix.
